name: Cerebras Systems
statusNote: IPO on Nasdaq Global Select (CBRS); priced 2026-05-13 at $185/share, began trading 2026-05-14, closed 2026-05-15. 34.5M shares incl. full overallotment, ~$6.38B gross proceeds. Closed day one at $311.07 (~$95B market cap per CNBC). Had filed Sept 2024, withdrew Oct 2025, refiled April 2026.
oneLiner: Wafer-scale AI processors (WSE-3) and an inference/training cloud built on them.
founders: Andrew Feldman (CEO; previously co-founded SeaMicro, sold to AMD) with Gary Lauterbach, Michael James, Sean Lie, Jean-Philippe Fricker (founder list from general knowledge, not re-verified in this pass)
research: Wafer-scale engine hardware line (WSE-1/2/3); open-source Cerebras-GPT models (older). Not deeply re-checked.
traction: FY2025 revenue $510.0M vs $290.3M in 2024 (424B4). Customer concentration: MBZUAI 62% and G42 24% of 2025 revenue. OpenAI cloud deal worth >$20B through 2028 (Jan 2026) and AWS deployment of Cerebras chips (Mar 2026) per CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/14/cerebras-cbrs-stock-trade-nasdaq-ipo.html).
compute: Owns its silicon and operates its own inference datacenters; AWS partnership.
moat: Proprietary wafer-scale silicon with a speed lead on inference; very hard to replicate.
risks: Heavy UAE customer concentration (MBZUAI + G42 = 86% of 2025 revenue); competes with Nvidia; public-market volatility.
notes: PUBLIC: exclude from the private ranking. IPO details are confirmed by the SEC 8-K and 424B4.

name: Databricks
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. CEO Ali Ghodsi said in June 2026 'this is a terrible year to go public' and in August pointed to 2027; no public S-1 on EDGAR as of early Oct 2026.
oneLiner: Lakehouse data and AI platform (Spark, Delta Lake, Lakebase, Genie, Unity AI Gateway) for enterprises.
founders: Ali Ghodsi (CEO), Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica, Reynold Xin, Patrick Wendell, Andy Konwinski, Arsalan Tavakoli-Shiraji; the Berkeley AMPLab creators of Apache Spark
talentSignals: Founders are the Berkeley creators of Spark; Ghodsi is still on UC Berkeley faculty (X bio).
research: Created and maintains major open source projects: Apache Spark, Delta Lake, MLflow (each well over 10k GitHub stars), plus Mosaic research and the DBRX model. Star counts not re-verified.
xPresence: CEO @alighodsi 216k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). The @databricks handle returned 404 on fxtwitter, so its follower count was not verified.
traction: $7B+ revenue run-rate with >80% YoY growth in its Q2 (Aug 2026); Lakebase above $100M run-rate. $5.4B run-rate in the January quarter, up 65%, and free-cash-flow positive (CNBC Feb 2026).
moat: Huge enterprise install base, data gravity and switching costs, open-source standards.
risks: Competition from Snowflake and the hyperscalers; IPO timing; valuation is about 27x run-rate.
notes: Arguably not an 'AI startup' in the narrow sense, but it is private. The Feb 2026 round letter (Series L) is unconfirmed; the round is labeled by amount only.

name: Modal
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026. Reportedly closing a $750M Accel-led round at a $15.75B post-money valuation (TechCrunch, 2026-09-28; not yet confirmed by the company).
oneLiner: Serverless GPU and CPU cloud for inference, training, batch jobs and code sandboxes, built on a custom container runtime and file system.
founders: Erik Bernhardsson (CEO; built Spotify's music recommendation system, ex-CTO Better.com, author of Annoy and Luigi); Akshat Bubna (CTO; MIT, early engineer at Scale AI)
talentSignals: Built its own file system and container runtime instead of using Kubernetes (General Catalyst interview, Sep 2026)
Stockholm team builds core infrastructure; London office opened in 2026 (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/erikbern_were-opening-an-office-in-london-im-personally-activity-7501346607825694720--vZ5)
research: Strong engineering blog output (GPU and inference benchmarks). Client OSS is modest (modal-labs/modal-client, about 520 stars).

xPosts.author: bernhardsson
xPosts.summary: CEO says he has zero interest in selling Modal and would 'just go build Modal 2 anyway'.

xPresence: CEO @bernhardsson 59.0k followers; @modal 37.5k; CTO @akshat_b 6.7k (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Erik is a well-known engineering blogger and poster.
traction: Annualized revenue about $300M (May 2026), up 5x from $60M in Sep 2025 (Reuters). Customers include Black Forest Labs, Legora and DoorDash (company LinkedIn post). Works with 13 cloud providers, up from 5 (Dealroom/Reuters).
compute: Aggregates GPU capacity from 13 cloud providers.
moat: Developer experience and custom runtime (sub-second container boots); sandbox product for AI-generated code.
risks: Resells third-party GPUs, so margins can be squeezed; competes with Baseten, Together, Fireworks and the hyperscalers.
notes: The $15.75B round was reported by TechCrunch with Axios/Bloomberg corroborating details, but it is not confirmed as closed, so latestValuation uses the confirmed $4.65B. Headcount not found.

name: Baseten
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026; in talks at about $26B (Axios, 2026-09-22; not closed).
oneLiner: Inference and post-training platform for running custom and open models in production for AI-app companies.
founders: Tuhin Srivastava (CEO), Amir Haghighat, Philip Howes, Pankaj Gupta; Australians, ex-Gumroad (founder backgrounds from general knowledge; Australian co-founders confirmed by Reuters)
talentSignals: Raised four rounds in 18 months (company blog).

rounds.leads: Altimeter, Conviction, Spark Capital (co-leads Sands, Wellington)

research: Engineering blog on inference optimization; little formal research.

xPosts.author: tuhinone
xPosts.summary: CEO shares the Series F announcement ($1.5B at $13B; revenue up 20x and inference volume up 40x in a year).

traction: Revenue up 20x and inference volume up 40x over the last year (Series F blog). Customers include Abridge, Clay, Cursor, Lovable, Mercor, OpenEvidence, Notion and Harvey (BusinessWire/Seedtable). The $600M annualized figure is from The Information via RevenueMemo.
compute: Multi-cloud GPU capacity; NVIDIA invested in the Series E.
moat: Inference performance engineering plus post-training workflow; sticky app-layer customers.
risks: Competitive inference market; GPU cost exposure; valuation momentum.
notes: ARR figures are secondary (The Information, relayed by RevenueMemo). The Series F included tranches at $13B and $11B. Headcount not found.

name: Together AI
statusNote: Private; raised an $800M Series C at $8.3B post-money in July 2026.
oneLiner: AI-native cloud for open-model inference, fine-tuning, RL and pre-training, plus research on AI efficiency.
founders: Vipul Ved Prakash (CEO), Ce Zhang, Chris Ré (Stanford), Percy Liang (Stanford); Tri Dao (FlashAttention author, Princeton professor) is Chief Scientist
talentSignals: Chief Scientist Tri Dao is the creator of FlashAttention and Mamba co-author (X bio confirms role)
research: Frontier efficiency research: FlashAttention (Dao-AILab/flash-attention, 25.1k GitHub stars), Mamba, RedPajama datasets, many papers at top venues from founders' labs.
traction: Annual bookings above $1.15B in Q2 2026; thousands of paying customers including Cursor, Cognition and Decagon; over 1M developers (BusinessWire).
compute: Commitments for 500+ MW of compute capacity, capitalized separately by new investors (company blog); NVIDIA is an investor.
moat: Research credibility (FlashAttention lineage) plus owned GPU clusters at scale.
risks: Capital-intensive GPU ownership; price competition in open-model inference.
notes: The $1B annualized revenue (Feb 2026) is a Sacra estimate; the company-stated metric is bookings. Headcount not found.

name: Fireworks AI
statusNote: Private; $1.505B Series D at $17.5B (July 2026). Reportedly exploring a round near $30B (The Information, Sep 2026; unconfirmed).
oneLiner: Platform for training, customizing and serving open-weight models (specialized intelligence) at scale.
founders: Lin Qiao (CEO; led PyTorch at Meta) and a team of ex-Meta PyTorch engineers (Reuters: 'founded by former Meta engineers')
talentSignals: Founding team built and ran PyTorch at Meta.
research: Inference engine and optimization work (FireAttention, custom kernels) published on its blog; limited OSS.

xPosts.author: FireworksAI_HQ

compute: Partnerships with Microsoft and NVIDIA (NVIDIA is an investor).
moat: Inference performance plus fine-tuning/RL platform; scale of specialized-model serving.
risks: Commoditizing inference pricing; model labs vertically integrating.
notes: Series C date (Oct 2025) is inferred from the BusinessWire 'related release'; confirm if needed. Headcount not found.

name: fal
statusNote: Private; in talks at $15B-$20B (The Information, 2026-09-25; unconfirmed).
oneLiner: Generative media cloud: fast APIs and infrastructure for image, video and audio generation models.
founders: Burkay Gur (ex-Coinbase, MIT CSAIL per X bio) and Gorkem Yurtseven (ex-Amazon; from general knowledge)
research: Inference optimization for diffusion models; blog posts. Limited formal research.
xPresence: @fal 68.1k followers; co-founder @burkaygur 7.2k (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Very active launch-day posting for new media models.
traction: Annualized revenue about $800M (Sep 2026), doubling roughly every six months. Customers include Adobe, Shopify and Canva (The Information via Sovereign Magazine).
moat: Speed and model breadth in generative media; developer distribution.

notes: The ~$8B spring 2026 round is reported (two tranches), not company-announced. Round stage letters for 2025 are from Sacra. Founded year and HQ from general knowledge.

name: Fluidstack
statusNote: Private; raised $1.5B led by Jane Street at $18B (Sep 2026).
oneLiner: Builds and operates large AI compute clusters and datacenters for frontier labs (Anthropic, Google TPU deployments).
founders: César Maklary and Gary Wu (Oxford spinout; Forbes says the founders are now billionaires). Names from general knowledge, not re-verified.
talentSignals: Hiring for 'hundreds of roles' (company Series A post).
xPresence: No company X handle found (fluidstackio, FluidstackAI and fluidstack all return 404 on fxtwitter). Quiet.

compute: Core business; tens of billions in project debt for datacenter construction (Dealroom).

name: Etched

oneLiner: Rack-scale 'frontier inference clusters' on custom silicon (the original transformer-only Sohu ASIC branding has been retired).

talentSignals: 400+ employees at stealth exit, about 15% ex-Nvidia (TechCrunch via temperature2)
First-pass silicon success on TSMC N4P within three years of seed (GlobeNewswire)

name: turbopuffer
statusNote: Private and profitable; raised under $1M total (Lachy Groom angel round, then a Dec 2025 seed with Thrive Capital).
oneLiner: Serverless vector and full-text search engine built on object storage, used for retrieval in AI products.
founders: Simon Hørup Eskildsen (CEO; ex-Shopify principal engineer on infrastructure) and Justine Li (CTO; ex-Shopify)
talentSignals: 37 employees serving about 1,200 customers on track for $100M+ revenue (Globe and Mail, 2026-07-03)
Eskildsen says turbopuffer is the biggest company by revenue ever to come out of Shopify (BetaKit)
research: Widely read technical blog on object-storage-native search architecture; small OSS clients only.
xPresence: @turbopuffer 17.2k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). The founder's handle @Sirupsen returned 404 on fxtwitter, so it was not verified.
traction: About $100M run-rate by Mar 2026 and profitable. Customers include Anthropic, Cursor, Notion, Atlassian, Legora and Bridgewater (BetaKit, Sacra, Globe and Mail).

risks: Hyperscalers and Postgres-based vector search could commoditize it; small team.
notes: No valuation disclosed. The $100M run-rate is a Sacra estimate echoed by Dealroom; the Globe and Mail says 'on track for US$100M+ revenue this year'.

Angels include Scott Wu (Cognition) and Igor Babuschkin (Bryk LinkedIn)

name: Reducto
statusNote: Private; latest announced round was a $75M Series B (Oct 2025). Forge Global reports an unannounced $51M Series B-1 (Aug 2026) at about $1.04B post, which the company has not confirmed.
oneLiner: Document intelligence API that combines OCR and vision-language models to parse, split, extract and edit complex documents for LLMs.
founders: Adit Abraham (CEO) and Raunak Chowdhuri (CTO); YC W24
talentSignals: Burned only about $1M from YC to Series B in 18 months (Multiples)
research: Agentic OCR and VLM document parsing; blog posts and benchmarks (RD-TableBench). No major OSS.
traction: 1B+ pages processed and hundreds of millions of pages per month as of Oct 2025 (6x monthly volume growth in 5 months). Customers include Harvey, Rogo, Mercor, Scale AI, a Fortune 10 company and top-5 hedge funds (Multiples). Acquired Opennote in May 2026 (PitchBook) and opened a NY office in Sep 2026.
moat: Accuracy on messy enterprise documents; enterprise trust.
risks: Frontier VLMs are commoditizing document parsing; competitors Datalab, LlamaParse, Mistral OCR.
notes: The Series A lead (Benchmark) and seed lead (First Round) are from memory/RevenueMemo context and should be verified. The $1.04B Series B-1 valuation is unconfirmed. Revenue figure is a Contrary estimate.

name: Datalab
statusNote: Private, seed-stage; no round after the $3.5M seed found as of Oct 2026.
oneLiner: Trains small, accurate document-intelligence models (Surya, Marker, Chandra) and sells a hosted API and on-prem licenses.
founders: Vik Paruchuri (CEO; previously founded Dataquest, author of marker/surya) and Sandy Kwon
talentSignals: Reached seven-figure ARR and 40k+ GitHub stars with a team of three (Paruchuri at AI Engineer, https://ai.engineer/talks/K-iYKDMFKhE-small-ai-teams-huge-impact-vik-paruchuri)
research: Major OSS: marker 40.3k stars, surya 21.5k, chandra 12.5k (GitHub API, 2026-10-09). Chandra OCR 2 (4B params, Mar 2026) reports a state-of-the-art 85.9% on the olmOCR benchmark.
traction: Seven-figure ARR (talk); Anthropic reported as a customer (idp-software.com, lower reliability). Weights licensed free below $2M revenue, paid above.
moat: Open-source mindshare plus small fast models; license model captures commercial users.
risks: Tiny team; frontier VLMs closing the gap; competitor Reducto has far more capital.
notes: PitchBook lists the seed as $3.4M (Aug 2024) with Factorial Capital; Forkable says $3.5M led by Pebblebed with Peak XV. No 2026 funding found.

name: Arcee AI
statusNote: Private; Series B announced 2026-09-16 valuing it at more than $1B (Fortune: $1B pre-money, at least $150M raised).
oneLiner: US lab training frontier open-weight models (Trinity family, including the 400B MoE Trinity Large) plus tools to customize and deploy them.
founders: Mark McQuade (CEO; Hugging Face alum per X bio); co-founders not re-verified
talentSignals: Trained its entire 2025 model lineup, including the 400B Trinity Large, for about $20M (GlobeNewswire)

traction: Trinity models used in agentic workflows (company); DOE and national-lab partnership; strategic investors Hitachi, M12 and Wipro.
moat: Capital-efficient training know-how; US open-weight positioning with DOE ties.
risks: Competes with Chinese open models and well-funded labs; revenue not disclosed.
notes: Round amount is not company-disclosed ('at least $150M' per a Fortune source). The postValuation of $1.15B is computed from $1B pre-money plus $150M and is approximate. Earlier rounds (2024 Series A) not re-verified.

name: Moondream
statusNote: Private; only known funding is a $4.5M pre-seed/seed (Oct 2024). No 2025-2026 round found.
oneLiner: Efficient open-weight vision-language models (Moondream 3.1, 9B MoE with 2B active) and a cloud API for detection, pointing, captioning and segmentation.
founders: Vik Korrapati (CTO, @vikhyatk) and Jay Allen (CEO); worked together at AWS for 8 years
research: Open-weight VLM line: moondream2 (1.9B) to Moondream 3 Preview (Sep 2025) to Moondream 3.1 (2026-07-07), with state-of-the-art claims on COCO, ODinW-13 and ChartQA. GitHub m87-labs/moondream has 10.1k stars.
